description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of four different methods—Greedy and RPG decoding applied to two model sizes, CodeLlama-7B and CodeLlama-34B—across three code generation evaluation metrics: EGP (higher is better), TR-N (lower is better), and CCP (higher is better). The vertical axis represents performance, scaled from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2. Each metric group contains four bars, color-coded as follows: blue for Greedy (CodeLlama-7B), orange for RPG (CodeLlama-7B), green for Greedy (CodeLlama-34B), and red for RPG (CodeLlama-34B). For EGP, RPG (CodeLlama-34B) achieves the highest performance (~0.99), followed by RPG (CodeLlama-7B) at ~0.89, Greedy (CodeLlama-34B) at ~0.59, and Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) near 0.0. In TR-N, Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) performs best (~0.70), followed by Greedy (CodeLlama-34B) at ~0.62, RPG (CodeLlama-7B) at ~0.46, and RPG (CodeLlama-34B) at ~0.41. For CCP, RPG (CodeLlama-34B) again leads (~0.94), followed by RPG (CodeLlama-7B) at ~0.72, Greedy (CodeLlama-34B) at ~0.70, and Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) at ~0.40. The chart visually emphasizes that RPG decoding generally improves performance over Greedy decoding, especially for the larger CodeLlama-34B model, and that performance trends vary significantly depending on the metric and model size.
